generated.title: M7.0 Tibet Earthquake: 16 Dead, 339 Homes Collapsed, Officials Say
generated.description:
Chinese authorities report at least 16 people killed and 32 injured, including 11 seriously, after a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Tibet, China, on October 22, 2026. At least 339 homes collapsed, according to the Nagqu city government, as cited by news agencies. Search and rescue operations are continuing. These figures are preliminary and may change.

The earthquake struck 191 km east-northeast of Nagqu at 22:33 local time (14:33 UTC), at a depth of 18 km, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). The event data has been reviewed by USGS. Magnitude is the USGS value (Mww); other agencies may publish different values.

USGS issued an orange PAGER alert for this earthquake. PAGER is a modeled estimate of potential impact. The casualty and damage figures above are reported by authorities, not PAGER estimates.

This is a follow-up to our first report on this earthquake: https://youtu.be/4ZrrJfRGJRQ

Sources:
- USGS: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us6000u43g
- AP via NBC: https://www.nbcnews.com/world/china/70-earthquake-hits-chinas-tibet-killing-16-injuring-32-rcna605100
- AFP via CBS: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/powerful-earthquake-tibet-china/
